Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the AeroDef Corporation Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. As a reminder, instructions for queuing up questions will be given at that time. Please note this event is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to John Smith, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

John Smith:
Thank you, Operator, and good morning, everyone. Welcome to AeroDef Corporation's Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. Joining me today are David Johnson, Chief Executive Officer; Sarah Lee, Chief Financial Officer; Mike Chen, Chief Operating Officer; Lisa Patel, Chief Technology Officer; Robert Kline, Chief Strategy Officer; Emily Rodriguez, Chief Marketing Officer; and Tom Harris, Chief Compliance Officer.

Before we begin, I'd like to remind you that this call contains forward-looking statements. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of risks and uncertainties.

David Johnson:
Thank you, John, and good morning. AeroDef Corporation delivered a solid performance in Q3, demonstrating the resilience of our business model and the strength of our diversified portfolio. Our priorities remain focused on executing our strategy, driving operational excellence, and delivering value to our shareholders. Today, we'll touch on key areas including free cash flow generation and utilization, capital deployment strategy, drivers of aftermarket performance, performance of priority defense programs, R&D investment in next-generation platforms and technologies, expansion of service offerings and customer base, defense budget outlook and impact on the company, and book-to-bill ratio overall and by segment.

We are particularly excited about the recent advancements in our NGAD program and its potential to enhance our air dominance capabilities and drive significant revenue growth in the years ahead. We are seeing strong demand for our defense systems, and our commercial aerospace business is recovering steadily.

Sarah Lee:
Thank you, David. Now, let's turn to the financials. In Q3, we reported revenue of $18.7 billion, representing a 12% increase year-over-year. Our earnings per share were $2.45. We continue to maintain a strong balance sheet with $4.2 billion in cash and equivalents. Our guidance for the full year remains unchanged at the top end. We are actively managing our costs and investing in key growth initiatives. We are also focused on returning capital to shareholders through dividends and share repurchases.

Our specific financial highlights include gross margin of 22.4%, operating income of $2.8 billion, and free cash flow of $1.4 billion.

Let me dive deeper into our free cash flow generation and utilization, which remains a cornerstone of our financial strength and strategic flexibility in the Aerospace & Defense sector. Free cash flow—or FCF—is calculated as cash from operations minus capital expenditures, underscoring our ability to fund growth, return capital to shareholders, and navigate the industry's cyclicality and long-lead program dynamics.

In Q3, we delivered FCF of $1.4 billion, a 56% increase year-over-year from $900 million in Q3 2023, and up 18% sequentially from Q2's $1.2 billion. This brings year-to-date FCF to $4.1 billion, putting us on track to hit the top end of our full-year guidance of $5.8 to $6.2 billion—well ahead of consensus estimates. Driving this is record operating cash flow of $2.1 billion, fueled by strong execution across our defense portfolio.

On the defense side, Aeronautics—anchored by low-rate initial production on Lot 18 F-35s and ramping Block 4 upgrades—generated $850 million in segment OCF, with cash conversion over 110% of adjusted EBITDA. Missile and Fire Control, benefiting from accelerated Hypersonic Attack Cruise Missile and Precision Strike Missile awards amid Indo-Pacific tensions, contributed $650 million, up 40% year-over-year, thanks to labor efficiencies. Space Systems added $450 million from GPS IIIF handovers and Vulcan Centaur milestones.

Commercial aerospace added $150 million—our best since pre-COVID—as 787 deliveries to Asia-Pacific picked up 25% quarter-over-quarter. Overall revenue growth, plus disciplined working capital—DSOs at 52 days from 58, inventory turns at 4.2x—freed up $1.2 billion more cash. We recovered $300 million in supplier advances from resolved titanium shortages, hit hard by post-Ukraine sanctions.

CapEx was $700 million, or 3.8% of sales, toward high-ROI areas: $250 million in digital thread using Siemens Teamcenter and Palantir for model-based engineering, cutting EAC variances 15% on B-21. $200 million to additive manufacturing for C-130J and JASSM-ER, slashing lead times 30%. U.S. DoD inflows surged 22% on $120 billion backlog acceleration from FY24 NDAA Ukraine aid, with international FMS from Poland and Saudi on Patriot adding $400 million.

On utilization, we prioritize balance sheet strength, growth, then returns. We've deployed $4.1 billion year-to-date: $1.2 billion net debt reduction to 1.8x net debt-to-EBITDA from 2.3x, refinancing $800 million notes at 3.8% saving $25 million yearly.

$1.5 billion into growth: $900 million self-funded R&D for hypersonics, HELIOS lasers, CCA drones. $400 million in supply chain resilience, new Huntsville composites center.

Shareholder returns: $800 million dividends—8% increase to $3.15 annualized, 62nd consecutive—and $600 million repurchases retiring 2.1% shares at $485, supporting 1.8% yield, 45% payout. Post-quarter, $3 billion ASR with Goldman from $7 billion authorization.

This FCF gives optionality amid labor shortages—we're 95% staffed—and fixed-price risks—65% cost-plus. Q4 FCF over $1.6 billion from F-35 Lot 19 and engines. $165 billion backlog—42 months coverage—moats us, with AI-optimized ERP and vendor inventory sustaining 95%+ conversion.

Turning to our capital deployment strategy, which is central to long-term shareholder value amid dynamic A&D conditions. We generated record FCF positioning us for dividends, repurchases, and acquisitions while investing in hypersonics, directed energy, next-gen space.

Priorities: strong balance sheet first, shareholder returns second, inorganic growth third. Ended with $4.2 billion cash, net debt 1.8x EBITDA below 2.5x target, $7.5 billion liquidity. Ratings A-/A3 intact from F-35 ramp to 180/year Lots 15-17, Virginia Block V. Reduced debt $500 million at sub-4% rates. FY24 FCF $4.0-4.3 billion with 12.5% margins.

Dividends top priority: 12% increase to $2.80 annual, $0.70 quarterly, 18th consecutive, 42% payout conservative vs. peers. 10% five-year CAGR, 2.2% yield. Resonates with surging budgets: U.S. $842 billion, NATO 2%+, Poland 4.1%, Japan/Australia P-8/MQ-25.

Repurchases: $1.7 billion FY23 retiring 2.1% at $385 below intrinsic. New $2.5 billion authorization to $3.2 billion through 2025, opportunistically below 14x EV/EBITDA.

Now, our book-to-bill ratio signals strong momentum. Overall 1.22x, $4.8 billion orders vs. $3.9 billion revenue, backlog $128 billion up 8%, 3.5 years coverage.

By segment: Defense Systems 1.35x, $2.1 billion bookings vs. $1.6 billion revenue from F-35 Lot 15, UK E-7, Asia F-X/KF-21. Missiles 1.48x, $1.7 billion vs. $1.1 billion from JASSM/PrSM Ukraine/Mideast, HAWC DARPA. Commercial 0.92x headwinds from 737/787/A320neo, but widebody wins. Space 1.12x from NASA CLPS, GPS IIIF, Vulcan.

Full-year guide 1.20-1.25x with capex $450 million for chains/IRAD.

Also, aftermarket grew 14% to $2.8 billion, 42% of sales, margins 28.5% up 220 bps from fleet utilization averaging 11.8 hours/day, 95% pre-COVID. Narrowbodies 12.5 hours, widebodies 9.2. Defense F-35 85%, helicopters 92%.

Maintenance: LEAP 28,000 cycles, light visits +15%, $450 million MRO. F-35 overhauls early, PBL $8 billion backlog. Regional: Americas 55%, EMEA 16%, APAC 20%.

EngineWise AI 95% accuracy, pricing +4%, base +5%. San Antonio MRO +$250 million robotic, F-35 ALIS. Guide Q4 12-15% growth, 27-28% margins.

Defense budget outlook robust: SIPRI $2.44 trillion 2023 up 6.8%, 4-5% CAGR. U.S. FY25 $849.8 billion up 4.1%, procurement +7.2%, RDT&E +2.3%. Europe NATO \u20ac380 billion +11%, Poland/Germany/UK. Indo-Pacific Japan $55 billion +8%, AUKUS/India. Mideast $150 billion.

Impacts us: defense bookings $4.2 billion vs. $3.8 billion revenue, backlog $28.5 billion. FY24 $24-25 billion +9%, 12.5% margins. 8-10% CAGR to 2027 from PrSM, NGAD, space.

Mike Chen:
Thank you, Sarah. Operationally, we've seen significant supply chain improvements, increasing production on key programs. We're investing in automation and digital tech for efficiency. Specifically, our priority defense programs drove over 65% bookings, margins 12.5% up 150 bps from cost discipline.

NGAD/F-35 Block 4: $2.1 billion revenue +18%, Lot 16 95% on-time DCUs, $2.8 billion bookings EOQ. Margins 13.8% open systems -22% integration. Sustainment 98% rates. International +25%.

Hypersonics ARRW/HACM: $850 million +32%, Mach 5+ tests unlock $1.5 billion FRP. Camden motors +40%, composites -15% costs. Margins 11.2%. AUKUS co-prod $3-5 billion potential.

IAMD NGI/PrSM: $1.4 billion +14%, $1.9 billion bookings. NGI kill tests, PrSM 120 units. Margins 14.1% scale. Poland PAC-3 $450 million.

CCA/space: $650 million CCA XQ-58A flights, $1.1 billion SDA Tranche 2. Margins 15.4% COTS. Backlog $48.7 billion +22%, 97% supplier OT. MBSE -35% cycles.

Exportability key, 15-20% int'l CAGR.

Lisa Patel:
Thank you, Mike. On technology, strides in next-gen propulsion. Specifically, Q3 R&D $1.45 billion, 11.8% revenue up 18%, full-year $5.8 billion 12.5% toward 12-14%.

Air dominance 42% $610 million: NGAD PCA digital twins, AI CFD -25%, adaptive engines 5:1 bypass, CCA Loyal Wingman F-35 teaming. $2.1 billion options.

Hypersonics/DE 28% $405 million: Mach 7 ARRW, CMCs +15% T/W, 300kW laser 95% vs UAVs HELIOS. AUKUS $4.5 billion.

Autonomy/space 22% $320 million: Mosaic 99.9% EW, ML -40% training, LEO optical 100 Gbps SDA $1.2 billion.

Enablers 8% $115 million: quantum, hybrid-electric 1,500 Wh/kg.

Regions: U.S. 85%, Europe 10% NATO/FCAS, APAC AUKUS $800 million, Mideast lasers. R&D:wins 1:4.2. FY25 +12-15%.

Robert Kline:
Thank you, Lisa. Strategically, evaluating acquisitions to complement portfolio. New models for opportunities. For instance, expansion of service offerings grew services 28% YoY to 42% revenue.

From OEM to services: DynTwin AI -35% maintenance, $320 million backlog 65%+ margins. Huntsville MRO F-35, PBL 95% rates $850 million +32%. SecureNet C4ISR $180 million Space Force.

Customer diversification: top 5 from 65% to 48%, 17 new logos, $4.2 billion awards 60% new. U.S. B-21 $1.1 billion, Europe Poland F-16 \u20ac450 million +25%. APAC RAAF A$750 million AUKUS, India Tejas $220 million +40%. Commercial Blue Origin $95 million, UAE drones $150 million.

Services 68% margins, 55% recurring $12.5 billion backlog. R&D $210 million autonomy. Guide 25-30% FY24 growth.

Emily Rodriguez:
Thank you, Robert. Marketing-wise, new branding resonates, digital channels boost awareness. Results include strong uptake in services campaigns targeting new defense and commercial clients, driving the diversification we discussed.

Operator:
Thank you. We will now begin the question and answer session. Our first question comes from Josh Friedman with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Josh Friedman:
Good morning. Can you provide more color on the free cash flow outlook into next year?

David Johnson:
Certainly, Josh. Our FCF engine remains strong, with Q4 over $1.6 billion and full-year top-end guidance well in sight. Backlog coverage and efficiencies position us for continued outperformance.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Maria Lopez with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Maria Lopez:
Hi, I'm curious about your capital deployment priorities amid M&A opportunities?

Sarah Lee:
Maria, balance sheet first at 1.8x leverage, then dividends up 12% and opportunistic buybacks below intrinsic value, with $3.2 billion capacity. M&A for tuck-ins in hypersonics and drones when values align.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Alex Kim with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Alex Kim:
Regarding the R&D investments in hypersonics and NGAD, any updates on milestones?

Lisa Patel:
Alex, NGAD PDR Q2 FY25, hypersonic LRIP Q4, with AUKUS co-dev advancing. Returns strong at 1:4.2 ratio, aligned to FYDP priorities.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Dana Patel with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Dana Patel:
Question about book-to-bill in defense segments?

Robert Kline:
Dana, defense at 1.35x to 1.48x, driven by F-35, missiles replenishment, international surges. Full-year 1.20-1.25x with $128 billion backlog.

David Johnson:
Thank you for your questions. In closing, I'm confident in our ability to navigate the current environment and deliver long-term value to our shareholders. We remain focused on our strategic priorities, operational excellence, and innovation.

John Smith:
Thank you for joining us today. This concludes our earnings call.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for participating. You may now disconnect.
